hints: A flow assigns a nonnegative amount to each directed edge, never exceeding its capacity.
The amount delivered to the sink equals total flow leaving the source.
Repeatedly find a residual path from source to sink and augment by its smallest remaining capacity.
analogy: Residual edges let you reroute earlier choices while increasing total transferred data.
example: If a path has residual capacities 4,7,3, it can carry 3 more units before one edge fills.
algorithm: Use Edmonds-Karp or Dinic on a residual graph. Find augmenting paths, update forward and reverse residual capacities, and stop when no path remains.
correctness: When no residual source-to-sink path exists, the vertices reachable from source define a cut whose capacity equals the current flow, proving it is maximum by max-flow min-cut.
complexity: O(V^2 E) time with Edmonds-Karp (Dinic is faster on typical inputs) and O(V+E) residual storage.
